cards.title: Quote a large order, then negotiate down to a paid test run
cards.summary: Anchoring on a large intended production volume gets small buyers serious treatment and can preserve bulk unit pricing on a 500-unit test order.
cards.use_when: Pricing and supplier negotiation: you want a small first run but need factory-level pricing and responsiveness.

cards.title: Vet Alibaba suppliers using trade assurance, verification and transaction history
cards.summary: A stack of platform signals — trade assurance, third-party verification, years in business, recent transaction counts, buyer geography and product specialization — to screen out scammers and middlemen.
cards.use_when: Supplier vetting during sourcing: narrowing a long list of Alibaba suppliers to a shortlist worth sampling.

cards.title: Run the outreach funnel and batch-contact shortlisted suppliers
cards.summary: Source hundreds of suppliers, narrow to 20-40 enquiries, then 3-5 samples, using Alibaba's favorites and bulk contact features.
cards.use_when: Sourcing pipeline management: you have a candidate pool and need to run outreach efficiently without wasting weeks.

cards.title: Order samples before committing — including the paid custom sample
cards.summary: Samples are the cheapest defect-prevention step in manufacturing, and a paid custom sample catches issues a free blank sample cannot.
cards.use_when: Pre-production product validation: before releasing a full production order and payment.

cards.title: Design your product through the manufacturer, not a CAD professional
cards.summary: Factory staff can usually produce dimension and graphic modifications from plain-English instructions and sketches, with Fiverr/Upwork as fallback for complex work.
cards.use_when: Product development and packaging design: you want a modified or differentiated product rather than a private-labeled generic.

cards.title: Use 30/70 payment terms and inspect before releasing the balance
cards.summary: Pay a deposit, retain the balance until an inspection report confirms quality, and prefer reversible payment methods on your first orders.
cards.use_when: Sourcing payment and quality control: the moment you must move money overseas and want protection against non-delivery or defects.

cards.title: Ship from factory to Amazon: air vs. sea, freight forwarder and duty
cards.summary: Airfreight is fast and expensive, sea freight is slow and cheaper but needs a forwarder and customs handling; duties narrow China's cost advantage.
cards.use_when: Fulfillment and inbound logistics: getting a finished production run from the factory into Amazon's warehouse.

cards.title: Source a differentiated product, not a private-labeled generic
cards.summary: Private-labeling existing Alibaba products is described as a worked-in-the-past tactic; the current approach is customizing or improving an existing category product.
cards.use_when: Product selection and differentiation strategy: deciding what to actually sell before contacting suppliers.

cards.title: Keep manufacturer communication professional and build a real relationship
cards.summary: Professional, well-written messages plus genuine relationship-building affect how factories prioritize and accommodate you over time.
cards.use_when: Supplier relationship management: ongoing communication and reorders with an overseas manufacturer.

cards.title: Reconstruct a real first-year FBA cost stack when planning launch budget
cards.summary: A documented first-year launch budget from a case study gives a concrete, line-item starting point for capital planning.
cards.use_when: Launch budgeting and cash planning: estimating how much capital a first private-label FBA product actually requires before any revenue.

cards.title: Generate brand-name ideas and run a preliminary conflict screen
cards.summary: A low-cost brand-asset workflow: AI-generated name, USPTO availability cross-check, AI design feedback, then Canva execution.
cards.use_when: Brand setup before launch: naming and basic logo/brand elements for a new Amazon product line.

cards.title: Build listings by improving on an existing successful competitor listing
cards.summary: Competitor listing teardown — photos, price, positioning — is the starting brief for differentiation in both product and listing.
cards.use_when: PDP and listing creation: writing titles, bullets and image sets for a new product in a category with established sellers.

cards.title: Screen supplier communication quality and profile depth before shortlisting
cards.summary: Beyond trade assurance and verification, the source reads company name, profile completeness, and equipment/market data to distinguish real factories from vague resellers.
cards.use_when: Supplier shortlisting: deciding which of many Alibaba candidates to spend sample and negotiation time on.

cards.title: Amazon P&L anatomy for a first-year FBA product (revenue, product cost, referral fee, FBA pick & pack)
cards.summary: How to build a per-month Amazon FBA profit statement and which cost lines to subtract to know whether a product actually earns money.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether a product can hit your target margin before you commit to an order, or reconciling a month's revenue against real profit.

cards.title: Inventory availability as the core driver of Amazon revenue growth
cards.summary: Why stockouts are the most expensive recurring mistake for a scaling Amazon seller and how reorder timing should be planned around demand, not around minimums.
cards.use_when: Planning reorder quantities and reorder timing for a product that is selling faster than expected, or diagnosing a revenue drop after a good month.

cards.title: Qualify manufacturer capacity, not just MOQ, before scaling orders
cards.summary: How asking suppliers about maximum monthly output prevents the growth ceiling that cost the case-study seller about $20,000.
cards.use_when: Negotiating with a supplier before or during a scale-up, or when choosing between staying with an existing manufacturer and adding a second one.

cards.title: Quality control between sample and bulk production run
cards.summary: Why approving a sample is not approval of the production run, and how a low-cost third-party inspection protects reviews.
cards.use_when: Arranging an overseas production run, or diagnosing a spike in returns, poor reviews or listing complaints after a new batch arrives.

cards.title: Title and bullet keyword construction for Amazon search
cards.summary: How to research search phrases and build an Amazon title where the exact primary search phrase appears first.
cards.use_when: Writing or rewriting an Amazon product title, bullet points and description for a new or underperforming listing.

cards.title: Amazon listing setup mechanics: existing listing vs. new listing
cards.summary: Step-by-step path through Seller Central for adding a product to an existing ASIN versus creating a brand-new listing.
cards.use_when: Setting up a new product in Amazon Seller Central, or choosing between piggybacking on an existing ASIN and building your own.

cards.title: Compare FBA and merchant fulfillment for the actual product
cards.summary: Evaluate delivery eligibility, total costs and operational capacity rather than assuming FBA guarantees higher sales.
cards.use_when: Deciding the fulfillment channel for a new Amazon listing, or comparing the cost of FBA fees against the sales benefit of Prime eligibility.

cards.title: Using Amazon ads and promo-clear listings to relaunch a stalled product
cards.summary: How the case-study seller used PPC, A+ content and a competitor's removal to jump from a stockout toward a record month.
cards.use_when: Planning a relaunch or ranking push after a stockout, or deciding how much ad spend to reinvest into an existing Amazon listing.

cards.title: Launch speed and review momentum as copycat defense
cards.summary: Why a fast, review-generating launch is presented as protection against manufacturers copying your product.
cards.use_when: Planning the launch timeline and early review-generation push for a new private-label product, or deciding whether to delay a launch.

cards.title: Prepare an entity-structure brief for the ecommerce business
cards.summary: Gather the operational facts needed to select a suitable entity and tax setup rather than copying a course example.
cards.use_when: Forming the legal entity for a new Amazon or ecommerce store, or deciding whether a new product line needs its own entity.

cards.title: EIN, seller's permit and separating business banking
cards.summary: The free federal and state registrations an online seller needs, plus why commingling business and personal money is risky.
cards.use_when: Setting up back-office paperwork before launching an Amazon store, or fixing banking hygiene after mixing personal and business spending.

cards.title: Keep Amazon launch expenses traceable and separate from personal spending
cards.summary: Record inventory, freight, advertising and software spend consistently during a launch.
cards.use_when: Choosing how to pay for a product business's build-out costs (inventory, ads, samples, tooling) to maximize rewards.

cards.title: Map the product and brand assets that need IP review
cards.summary: Identify brand identifiers, appearance and technical features before deciding what protection to investigate.
cards.use_when: Deciding what intellectual property to file before applying for Amazon Brand Registry, or protecting a product design from copycats.

cards.title: Choosing an Amazon category and item type for your listing
cards.summary: How to pick the category and item-type keyword that determines where your product can rank.
cards.use_when: Filling in the category and item type fields while creating a new Amazon listing, or reconsidering the category of an existing listing.

cards.title: Reading keyword lists critically: choose specific buyer language over generic buzzwords
cards.summary: A filtering method for turning a raw keyword list into title and bullet terms that can actually rank.
cards.use_when: Editing a keyword list before writing Amazon title, bullets or description copy.

cards.title: Bullet points: lead with product name + benefits, not features
cards.summary: Structure Amazon bullet points so the primary keyword appears first and each bullet translates a feature into a concrete customer outcome.
cards.use_when: Writing or rewriting the five bullet points on an Amazon listing (PDP copy) for a consumable or any private-label product.

cards.title: Make the main image differentiate on the search results grid
cards.summary: Winning the click depends on packaging and main-image choices that stand out against competitors' thumbnails on Amazon search.
cards.use_when: Designing product packaging and the main listing image before launch so the product is clickable in search results.

cards.title: Use all eight side images to sell what buyers can't touch
cards.summary: Supplementary images substitute for the physical product experience and should include a comparison chart against competitors.
cards.use_when: Building the image gallery and A+ assets for an Amazon product page before or after launch.

cards.title: Fill product details thoroughly and consistently
cards.summary: Completing Amazon's product-detail attributes accurately (manufacturer, unit count, ingredients, expiration) prevents listing errors and improves discoverability.
cards.use_when: Creating a new Amazon listing and filling out the product-details section for a consumable or physical good.

cards.title: Price at 3x cost and position premium, not cheapest
cards.summary: The source recommends a minimum 3x markup over unit cost and pricing above competitors to signal quality and protect margin.
cards.use_when: Setting the launch price for a private-label Amazon product after calculating FBA fees.

cards.title: Use hidden listing attributes and a future offer start date for launch
cards.summary: Filling all attributes and setting a future offer start date lets you control launch timing and capture back-end discoverability fields.
cards.use_when: Finishing a new Amazon listing before hitting 'save and finish' and planning the launch day.

cards.title: Read Seller Central's home and inventory signals for restock timing
cards.summary: Daily Seller Central metrics (restock days-left, recommended quantity, buy box, open orders) drive replenishment decisions.
cards.use_when: Managing day-to-day operations and deciding when to reorder and ship replenishment inventory.

cards.title: Diagnose performance with Business Reports: sales, page views, conversion
cards.summary: Use Business Reports (sales & traffic) to separate traffic changes from conversion changes over time.
cards.use_when: Reviewing weekly or monthly store performance to decide whether to work on traffic or on conversion.

cards.title: Protect account health and address negative reviews
cards.summary: Monitor account-health issues separately from product reviews and resolve customer problems through permitted channels.
cards.use_when: Routine account maintenance and when a negative review or defect claim appears.

cards.title: Activate Brand Referral Bonus to offset fees on off-Amazon traffic
cards.summary: Brand Registry sellers earn back roughly 10% of sales driven from external traffic to their Amazon listing.
cards.use_when: Running off-Amazon ads, influencer posts, or email campaigns that send buyers to your Amazon listing.

cards.title: Create a case-pack template with correct box dimensions and weight
cards.summary: Before shipping to FBA, define a reusable case-pack template meeting Amazon's size/weight limits.
cards.use_when: Preparing the first FBA shipment or changing how you pack units into cases.

cards.title: Label units with FNSKU yourself or via manufacturer, not Amazon
cards.summary: Apply FNSKU labels before shipping; having Amazon label costs about $0.50/unit and is avoidable.
cards.use_when: Preparing units for an FBA shipment, especially private-label or wholesale/arbitrage products.

cards.title: Choose small parcel vs less-than-truckload by shipment size
cards.summary: Match the FBA shipping method to volume — small parcel for boxes, LTL/pallet for large shipments — to cut freight cost.
cards.use_when: Selecting a shipping method and carrier when creating an FBA shipment.

cards.title: Double-check box labels: weight, dimensions, and addresses
cards.summary: Errors on shipment labels cause lost inventory, fees, and carrier surcharges — verify before dispatch.
cards.use_when: After generating FBA box labels and before handing packages to the carrier.

cards.title: Track FBA shipments and reclaim lost inventory with documentation
cards.summary: Monitor shipment statuses and keep all paperwork to recover the value of lost or mis-received units.
cards.use_when: After sending inventory, while it's in transit and being received, and if quantities don't match.

cards.title: Ship inventory 3–6 weeks ahead and avoid stockouts
cards.summary: FBA check-in can lag weeks, so plan replenishment with a buffer and never assume urgency speeds it up.
cards.use_when: Planning replenishment timing and launch timing for FBA products.

cards.title: Keep shipment paperwork and the carrier receipt for FBA pallets
cards.summary: Retain the bill of lading and the driver's pickup receipt for every FBA pallet so you can prove shipment if Amazon reports inventory missing.
cards.use_when: Fulfillment: preparing or dispatching an FBA pallet shipment and setting up your record-keeping for inbound inventory.

cards.title: Call the carrier and pickup location the day before an FBA pallet pickup
cards.summary: Confirm truck type, liftgate or forklift needs, dock access and arrival window the day before pickup to avoid failed collections.
cards.use_when: Fulfillment: scheduling a pallet pickup from a home, warehouse or manufacturer for FBA inbound.

cards.title: Send roughly three to six months of FBA inventory and reorder at two to three months
cards.summary: Keep FBA stock between about three and six months of cover so you avoid both monthly storage and long-term storage fees and out-of-stock rank damage.
cards.use_when: Replenishment: deciding how many units to ship into FBA on each inbound and when to trigger the next production order.

cards.title: Optimize the search-result click drivers: main image, title keywords, price and review count
cards.summary: Amazon ranks on click-through and conversion, so tune the only elements shoppers see in search results and put your target keywords into the title.
cards.use_when: Product listing/SEO: creating or refreshing an Amazon listing title and main image before and during launch.

cards.title: Build launch-day sales velocity because Amazon rewards early sales spikes
cards.summary: Concentrate sales into launch day and the first weeks to signal demand and trigger a ranking snowball, since the top search positions take most sales.
cards.use_when: Acquisition: planning a new Amazon product launch and setting launch-day sales targets.

cards.title: Warm an audience before launch with social content plus an email waitlist
cards.summary: Post niche content on TikTok/Instagram/Facebook/YouTube, funnel viewers to an email waitlist, and email the list on launch day.
cards.use_when: Acquisition: building pre-launch demand and a launch-day traffic source for a new Amazon product.

cards.title: Run a pre-launch Facebook group to get product feedback and build commitment
cards.summary: A Facebook group beats a pure email list because members interact, give product feedback, and feel committed to buying at launch.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/merchandising: gathering buyer input on a product before finalizing it and creating a launch-day audience.

cards.title: Recruit small influencers with free product and use a podcast to build relationships
cards.summary: Find 5,000–10,000-follower creators in your niche, offer free product for a post, and interview influencers on your podcast so they reciprocate with promotion.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/creative strategy: sourcing creator content and launch-day traffic for an Amazon product without a paid ad budget.

cards.title: Use Amazon Live and one-click shoppable video to convert viewers directly
cards.summary: Amazon Live puts an influencer talking about your product next to a buy link, so viewers purchase in one click while watching.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/creative strategy: adding a live or video shopping channel to a launch plan or ongoing traffic mix.

cards.title: Collect authentic Amazon reviews without incentives or review gating
cards.summary: Use permitted feedback channels while keeping compensation, relationships and review sentiment out of solicitation.
cards.use_when: Launch/retention strategy: deciding whether to pursue review velocity through incentivized purchases and outdoor recruiting.

cards.title: Start with an automatic Amazon PPC campaign, then move to manual targeting
cards.summary: Automatic campaigns let Amazon pick relevant keywords while you learn what converts, then manual keyword campaigns become more profitable.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/paid search: launching Amazon advertising for a new or newly launched product.

cards.title: Use negative keywords and relevance to avoid paying for junk clicks
cards.summary: Negative keywords block searches where your ad would spend money without selling, and only relevant search phrases should receive your bids.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/paid search: managing an Amazon PPC campaign's spend and search-term report after launch.

cards.title: Enroll in Brand Registry for A+ content, video and conversion lift
cards.summary: Brand Registry unlocks A+ content pages, product videos and other modules that raise listing conversion, which in turn supports ranking.
cards.use_when: Product page/merchandising: building or upgrading an Amazon detail page and deciding which Brand-Registry-only modules to use.

cards.title: Apply for Brand Registry with a trademark and a product listing in place
cards.summary: You need a pending or registered trademark, ownership verification and an active seller account, plus an existing ASIN and a branded product image.
cards.use_when: Brand setup: preparing a Brand Registry application before or shortly after launching an Amazon product.

cards.title: Use Brand Registry protections and programs to stop hijackers and cut fees
cards.summary: Evaluate brand protection and marketing programs individually, using current eligibility and charges.
cards.use_when: Retention/risk management: ongoing account and listing protection once a branded product is selling on Amazon.

cards.title: Read Brand Analytics and Attribution to see who buys and where traffic comes from
cards.summary: Brand Registry unlocks search-term, demographic and cross-purchase reports plus Amazon Attribution for off-Amazon campaigns.
cards.use_when: Measurement: diagnosing which queries, audiences and off-Amazon channels produce Amazon sales.

cards.title: Apply Cialdini's six principles of influence to Amazon launch assets
cards.summary: Reciprocity, scarcity, authority, consistency, liking and consensus can each be mapped to a concrete pre-launch and listing tactic.
cards.use_when: Acquisition/offer design: assembling launch messaging, promotions and PDP elements for a new Amazon product.

cards.title: Set Up an Automatic Sponsored Products Campaign Inside Out (Split by Targeting Group)
cards.summary: Launch one auto campaign and split close match, loose match, substitutes and compliments into separate ad groups so each match type gets its own bid and its own performance data.
cards.use_when: You are launching Amazon PPC for a new or existing ASIN and want a beginner-safe automatic campaign you can later read and optimize.

cards.title: What Each Amazon Automatic Targeting Group Actually Matches
cards.summary: Understand close match, loose match, substitutes and compliments so you can decide which automatic groups deserve budget and which to switch off.
cards.use_when: You are deciding which automatic targeting groups to enable or how much to bid on each when launching or cleaning up an Amazon auto campaign.

cards.title: Build Keyword Lists With Magnet: Filtering Rules for Low-Competition Terms
cards.summary: Use the Magnet keyword tool to harvest hundreds of buyer search terms, then filter out head terms and irrelevant queries to build a targetable keyword list.
cards.use_when: You are building the keyword list for a manual Amazon Sponsored Products campaign or deciding which search terms your listing title and bullets should cover.

cards.title: Manual Keyword Targeting: Broad, Phrase and Exact Match Explained With Ads Implications
cards.summary: Set up a manual keyword campaign and choose broad, phrase or exact match knowing exactly what searches each will trigger and when negative keywords become mandatory.
cards.use_when: You are creating a manual Sponsored Products keyword campaign or diagnosing why a keyword campaign is burning spend on irrelevant search terms.

cards.title: Split Keyword Campaigns Into Themed Ad Groups to See What Makes Money
cards.summary: Organise manual keyword campaigns into topic-based ad groups so you can attribute profit to themes rather than reading one blended number.
cards.use_when: You are structuring manual Amazon PPC campaigns for a product with several distinct buyer intents or sub-audiences.

cards.title: Product Targeting Ads: Run on Competitor Detail Pages (and Group by Competitor to Read Profitability)
cards.summary: Create manual product-targeting Sponsored Products campaigns that place your ad on chosen competitor listings, and split ad groups by brand so you learn which competitor placements pay.
cards.use_when: You want to intercept demand on competitor PDPs or refine a broad category-targeting campaign.

cards.title: Negative Keywords in Amazon PPC: Exclude Mismatched Formats Before You Spend
cards.summary: Add negative keywords to every campaign so ads don't show for search intent your product cannot satisfy — starting with format and variant mismatches.
cards.use_when: You are launching or optimising any Amazon Sponsored Products campaign and want to reduce wasted clicks on non-buyers.

cards.title: Target Amazon Keywords by Reverse-Engineering Competitor ASINs (Cerebro / Reverse ASIN)
cards.summary: Pull a competitor's ASIN into a reverse-ASIN tool to see the exact search terms that lead shoppers to find and buy that listing, then build your own target list.
cards.use_when: You are choosing keywords for a new listing, validating product demand, or benchmarking your keyword coverage against a competitor's.

cards.title: Validate Demand Before You Buy Inventory: Sales Estimator, BSR and Fee Calculator
cards.summary: Estimate a product's monthly revenue and profit before committing inventory by converting BSR with a sales estimator and running the numbers through a fee calculator.
cards.use_when: You are evaluating a product opportunity and need to check whether units sold, price and Amazon's cut leave real profit.

cards.title: Find Product Opportunities by Filtering Revenue, Review Count and Category (Blackbox)
cards.summary: Use a product database tool with explicit filters for monthly revenue, review ceiling and category to generate a candidate list instead of browsing randomly.
cards.use_when: You are searching for a product to launch and want a shortlist that matches your revenue target and competitiveness tolerance.

cards.title: Pre-Launch Validation With Crowdfunding and Pre-Sales
cards.summary: Reduce the risk of ordering inventory for an unproven product by selling it before manufacturing it, using crowdfunding or similar pre-sale validation.
cards.use_when: You are about to place a first production order for a new product and want evidence people will buy before you commit capital.

cards.title: Compare FBA and merchant fulfillment for the actual product
cards.summary: Evaluate delivery eligibility, total costs and operational capacity rather than assuming FBA guarantees higher sales.
cards.use_when: You are deciding how to fulfil a product or considering switching an FBM listing to FBA to lift sales.

cards.title: Invest in Branding and Packaging Quality Instead of $5 Designs
cards.summary: Cheap logos and packaging suppress conversion on Amazon because shoppers judge the product's credibility from the visual assets before reading copy.
cards.use_when: You are budgeting for product design, logo, packaging or listing imagery before launch or relaunch.

cards.title: Launch Velocity: Why Early Sales Volume Shapes Amazon Search Placement
cards.summary: Aim to generate concentrated sales in the launch window because Amazon's ranking rewards early sales with higher search placement, and higher placement compounds into more clicks.
cards.use_when: You are planning a product launch window or deciding how much PPC and promotion budget to front-load on a new ASIN.

cards.title: Choosing Between Helium 10 and Jungle Scout: A Function-by-Function Comparison
cards.summary: Pick your Amazon tool stack by which specific capabilities you need — Helium 10 for breadth of research, listing and PPC automation, Jungle Scout for its supplier database.
cards.use_when: You are choosing which paid Amazon research tool to subscribe to, or deciding whether a second tool is justified.

cards.title: Using a Listing Analyser and Index Checker to Diagnose Conversion and Rank Gaps
cards.summary: Score your listing against competitors and check which keywords you actually index for, so you can fix the specific weakness instead of rewriting blindly.
cards.use_when: An Amazon listing is getting impressions but weak conversion, or you want to confirm you rank for the keywords you are bidding on.

cards.title: Recover Amazon's Own Errors and Protect Inventory With Operations Tools
cards.summary: Run scheduled checks that claw back money Amazon owes you and guard against listing hijackers and stockouts, since both quietly destroy Amazon margin.
cards.use_when: You are operating an existing Amazon listing and want to reduce leakage in fees, reimbursements and inventory continuity.

cards.title: Commit Budget to Tools Early Rather Than Trialling Everything Manually
cards.summary: The source argues that refusing to spend on tooling early is itself the expensive choice, because manual guesswork leads to larger downstream mistakes.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether to pay for Amazon research, listing or PPC tooling on a tight starting budget.

cards.title: Amazon Referral Fees and Unit Economics: Start With the 15% Cut
cards.summary: Before locking a price, model the referral fee as a percentage of sale price plus per-unit fulfilment cost so a healthy-looking price still leaves profit.
cards.use_when: You are setting or revising a product price, or checking whether a sourced product can be profitable at the price the market supports.
